# Basics

## Common Aesthetics

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Multiple aesthetic choices
    - Some convey only qualitative information (shapes)
    - Some convey quantitative information (position, size, color [qual and quant])

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("common-aestheticss", fig_common_aesthetics(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Position

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Cartesian coordinates
    - 2D: x and y
    - Specify range
    - Units (label)
    - Scales should match if x and y are the same unit   
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("cartesian-coordinates", fig_cartesian_coordinates(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 1.2, width = 5)
place_fig("fig-temp-houston", fig_temp_houston(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 5, width = 5)
```

::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::


## Color

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Convey both qualitative and quantitative information
    - Qualitative: categorical variables
    - Quantitative: continuous variables
    - Qualitative scales should be distinct and easily distinguishable

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("qual-color", qual_color(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 7, y = 2, width = 8.5)
```
## Color

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Quantitative color scales
    - Sequential: single hue, light to dark for intensity
    - Diverging: two hues, light to dark for difference from a midpoint
      
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("quant-color-seq", quant_color_seq(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 1.4, width = 5)
place_fig("quant-color-div", quant_color_div(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 5, width = 5)
```
